definition.name: Software Factory default workflow
definition.description: The happy path of the factory: an idea is clarified into a PRD, designed, architected, implemented, tested, and delivered. Every state that produces a decision-bearing artifact stops for human approval before the workflow advances.
notes: A state advances only after its required artifacts exist, validate against their schema, and (when requiresApproval is true) are approved.
Failures are not states. They are a property of the run (status, attempt, last_error) so that a failed attempt never loses its place in the workflow. See workflow-design.md, 'Failure and retry'.
owner ids match file basenames under .opencode/agents/.
input.artifacts entries carry a required flag. Only required inputs must be produced by an earlier state; optional inputs are context the orchestrator supplies when it exists.

allowedActions vocabulary: readArtifacts, writeArtifact, writeTests, writeSource, runTests, askUser, readMemory, writeMemory. 'approve' is deliberately absent: only the orchestrator finalizes approval.

capability vocabulary: network, shell, sourceWrite, testExecution, packageInstall. A capability is what the execution environment grants a run, not what an agent is allowed to want. requiresCapabilities is unmet capability handling is declared per agent as fallbackWhenUnavailable; when absent, an unmet requirement blocks the run.

executionProfile names a runtime profile in packages/agent-runtime: which image, which paths are writable, which network mode, and whether package installation is allowed. A profile is a policy; the execution backend either applies it or refuses.
An agent proposes an artifact. The orchestrator validates it, persists it, and owns status and approved. See agent-protocol.md section 10.

completion.* declares what must be true before a state may be left. The orchestrator gathers the facts and packages/workflow evaluates them; no file outside the definition knows what any particular state requires.

IMPLEMENTATION requires an approved change proposal *and* an applied one. Approval is a statement about a diff; application is a statement about the project. Treating them as one requirement would let the workflow advance over code that is still in a workspace.
QA accepts a conditional test report only with a recorded human override. The verdict itself is not a workflow fact — whether an unverified result may pass is a policy, and it is declared.

IMPLEMENTATION leaves on `accepted`, not on `approved`. A reviewer who agrees to a diff has not accepted the finished product, and the two decisions are recorded separately: see IMPLEMENTATION.completion.
There is no QA state on the delivery path. Final acceptance of the built project is a human decision bound to a project commit.

product-manager.name: Product Manager
product-manager.responsibility: Turn a vague idea into confirmed, testable product requirements.

designer.name: Product Designer
designer.responsibility: Turn approved requirements into screens, flows, and interaction behaviour.

architect.name: Software Architect
architect.responsibility: Decide the technology stack, component boundaries, and contracts, then break the work into tasks.

frontend-developer.name: Frontend Developer
frontend-developer.responsibility: Implement approved frontend tasks against the approved design and API contracts.

backend-developer.name: Backend Developer
backend-developer.responsibility: Implement approved backend tasks against the approved API and data contracts.

qa-agent.name: QA Agent
qa-agent.responsibility: Verify the implementation against the approved acceptance criteria and report the result with evidence.

skillNotes.test-driven-development: Writing new test cases; see its writing-good-tests.md reference.
skillNotes.deliver-acceptance-criteria: Turning an approved criterion into a verifiable Given/When/Then scenario. Written for QA sign-off.
skillNotes.api-design-principles: Only for projects with a server: checking the implementation against the approved API contracts.
skillNotes.accessibility: Only for projects with a user interface: checking the shipped UI against WCAG 2.2 AA.

fallbackWhenUnavailable.note: Missing infrastructure is not an agent failure and not a hallucination. The honest report is a conditional verdict listing the criteria it could not exercise. An unavailable capability must never be recorded as a failed QA run.

boundaries.reason: A bug the agent fixes itself is a bug nobody sees. QA reports defects; the developers repair them.

states.title: Project created
states.purpose: A workspace exists and the user has stated an idea. No agent has been involved yet.

states.title: Product discovery
states.purpose: Turn a vague idea into confirmed requirements: problem, users, scope, constraints, open questions.

states.title: Product requirements
states.purpose: Produce the authoritative product specification, with testable acceptance criteria.

states.title: Design
states.purpose: Describe screens, flows, and interactions at the fidelity the project needs.

skip.reason: Projects with no user interface do not need a design.

states.title: Architecture
states.purpose: Decide the technology stack, components, contracts, and deployment, then break the work into tasks.

states.title: Implementation
states.purpose: Write the source code for the approved tasks, inside the isolated project environment.

artifacts.note: the reviewer's own words, when they asked for changes. This is the whole of what a human said, kept as written — it is the correction's instruction, and it is written by a person rather than by an agent, so it is not shaped like a document.

approvalScope: whether the work is accepted into the project

execution.parallelism: per task, only for tasks declared independent by the architect

override.reason: the product is accepted by a person or it is not delivered

requirements.note: a human agreed to a diff. This is not the same decision as accepting the finished product, which is the next requirement, and it does not satisfy it.
the built software, accepted by a person, at the commit they were shown. A successful agent run cannot satisfy this and neither can an approved diff.

notes: requiresApproval is false here because this state approves no document. Its human gates are two distinct decisions, and keeping them distinct is the point: a reviewer who agrees to one commit's diff has not thereby accepted the product, and the workflow must not record that they had.
`accepted` is the gated event. It is what a person means by accepting a project, and it requires the four requirements above: work produced, work reviewed, work applied, product accepted.

IMPLEMENTATION -> IMPLEMENTATION on `changes_requested` is a human-requested correction, not an automated loop. Nothing enters it on its own; the engineer's next run exists only because someone asked for one, and control returns to that person afterwards.

states.title: Quality assurance
states.purpose: Verify the implementation against the approved acceptance criteria and report the result honestly.

artifacts.note: the previous report, used to re-test known failures and catch regressions

invocation.note: The agent may write tests and reports, and may run the project's test command. It may not write under source/; see agents['qa-agent'].boundaries.

override.reason: a conditional test report is accepted or refused by a human

notes: QA is not part of the MVP delivery path. Autonomous verification was attempted and removed: it cost more model budget than it returned and, when it worked, its verdict was a second opinion about work a person had already reviewed. Nothing transitions into this state and DONE does not require its report.
The state is kept rather than deleted so that the contract, the schema and the agent remain available as an explicit, opt-in experiment. See notes.deferredContracts for what else is parked.
Final acceptance of the built project is a human decision recorded against a project commit; see IMPLEMENTATION.completion and the `acceptance` requirement kind.

states.title: Delivered
states.purpose: The project is delivered. Nothing further is expected of the agents.

artifacts.note: the reviewer's last words, kept as history. DONE requires no document.

notes: DONE is reached by a recorded human acceptance of the built project, not by a document and not by a test report. The acceptance is bound to the project commit, so a project that changes afterwards is no longer delivered.

transitions.note: a human asked for changes. Not an automatic loop: the engineer's run happens because someone requested one, and control returns to that person when it is applied.
a person accepted the built project at the commit they were shown
